topic: moral licensing -- why buying 'eco-friendly' products makes people cheat more
title: Why Buying 'Eco-Friendly' Products Makes People Lie And Steal More
description: Ever wonder why doing one 'good' thing can make you feel free to do something bad right after? This is AI-narrated original commentary exploring the psychology of moral licensing -- not a reaction, reupload, or summary of anyone else's video. #shorts #psychology

hook_candidates.text: People who buy 'eco-friendly' products are more likely to lie and steal right after.
Why do people who just did something good sometimes feel free to do something bad right after?
Doing something virtuous doesn't make you more virtuous going forward -- often it does the opposite.
In one study, shoppers who picked 'green' products over regular ones were later caught lying and stealing more, not less.

beats.text: Buying **eco-friendly** products makes you more likely to **lie** and steal right after.
Green shoppers in the study cheated and **stole** more.
Researchers say the product **didn't matter** -- feeling like a good person already did.
That's **moral licensing** -- one good purchase, permission to misbehave. Noticed that in you?
